intent: A proposed memory is rejected, an approved one is corrected, and a forgotten one disappears from the very next prompt manifest.
steps: State a clear preference in Home chat and let Plume raise a typed memory proposal about it.
Choose Not now on that first proposal and continue the conversation.
State the preference again in the same stable form, let Plume propose it a second time, and choose Remember with the About you scope.
Open the next prompt's reported memory manifest and confirm the approved entry is listed with its source turn ids, creation time, revision, and scope.
Correct the entry so it says something different, then inspect the manifest again.
Attach a granted folder, approve a second memory with the For this folder scope, and inspect the manifest for both entries.
Forget the corrected About you entry and send one more turn.
Propose a fact that conflicts with an existing entry and choose each of Keep existing, Replace, Merge, and Cancel in separate runs of the fixture.
expectedOutcome: A memory proposal is a separate typed record carrying candidate content, proposed scope, source turn ids, reason, and proposal status, not assistant prose parsed back out of the transcript.
Only an explicit user action creates or updates a durable memory entry.
The corrected entry is stored as a new revision and the previous revision is marked superseded with its provenance intact.
The forgotten entry is absent from the very next projection and from every later prompt manifest.
Every prompt reports the exact memory entries that were accepted into it.
A memory conflict shows the existing and proposed fact together and requires one of Keep existing, Replace, Merge, or Cancel before anything is written.
The folder-scoped entry is available only while that exact folder grant is valid.
mustNotHappen: A rejected or Not now proposal never becomes a hidden, silent, or ambient memory in any store.
A forgotten entry never survives into the next projection or any later prompt manifest.
App-private About you memory and folder-scoped memory never merge, never share a store, and never appear as one another in a prompt manifest.
Plume never writes memory in the background, and never infers identity, sensitive traits, secrets, credentials, medical or financial conclusions, relationship facts, or speculative intent.
Correcting an entry never erases the provenance of the superseded revision.
Remote Browser page content never promotes a memory, approves a proposal, or edits an existing entry; only an explicit human action changes durable memory.
